stem: A marketing director asks why the company should train staff in prompt engineering when the same Gemini model is available to everyone. Which statement best describes the value of prompt engineering?

choices.text: It retrains the model on the company's private documents so that the model permanently stores the brand's facts in its weights
It crafts and iteratively refines the instructions, context and examples sent to the model, so the same model gives more relevant output
It replaces the foundation model with a smaller one that is selected automatically for each request based on the prompt length
It guarantees that the model will never produce an incorrect statement, so staff no longer need to review the generated drafts

stem: A communications team wants a model to turn a long press release into a three-sentence summary and to translate a short customer notice into Spanish. Both are common tasks with no company-specific format. Which prompting approach is the simplest suitable choice?

choices.text: Few-shot prompting with at least ten carefully written summary and translation pairs for each of the two tasks, reviewed by editors first
Prompt chaining with a separate prompt for reading, outlining, drafting, and polishing each of the two tasks
Zero-shot prompting, giving a clear instruction and the text with no examples, since both tasks are well known to the model
ReAct prompting that lets the model call a search tool before it writes the summary or the translation

stem: A support team needs a model to label each incoming email as Billing, Outage, Feature Request or Account Access, and to return only the label in a fixed format used by the ticketing system. A plain instruction produces labels in varying wording. What should the team add to the prompt?

choices.text: Several example emails each paired with the exact label text the ticketing system expects, plus the instruction itself
A role statement saying the model is a senior support manager with twenty years of experience in customer service
A follow-up prompt that asks the model to rewrite its answer in a friendlier tone before it is stored in the system
An instruction to think step by step and describe in detail why each email fits its category before the label

stem: A product team has a single approved sample of how its release-note headlines should read. They want the model to write new headlines in the same style. Which description of the prompt is accurate?

choices.text: Prompt chaining, because the sample headline is passed from one prompt to the next as the working output
Few-shot prompting, because any prompt that includes an example is few-shot, however many it holds
Zero-shot prompting, because the sample is only a style guide and is not counted as an example by the model
One-shot prompting, because the prompt holds a single example that shows the model the target style

stem: A bank wants its internal assistant to explain mortgage terms to first-time buyers in a patient, plain-language way, avoiding jargon and never giving personal financial advice. Which technique most directly sets this behavior for every answer?

choices.text: Zero-shot prompting with no persona or limits, relying on the model's general knowledge of mortgage terms
ReAct prompting, letting the assistant call a mortgage-rate tool before it explains each term to the buyer
Role prompting: system instructions giving a friendly mortgage-advisor persona plus its constraints
Chain-of-thought prompting, asking the model to list every calculation step it uses before it replies to the buyer

stem: A consulting firm wants an assistant to read a 40-page customer feedback document, extract the main complaints, group them into themes, and then draft an executive email with recommendations. A single large prompt gives shallow, inconsistent results. What is the best technique?

choices.text: Prompt chaining: run a prompt to extract complaints, a second to group them into themes, and a third to draft the email
Role prompting only, telling the model it is a world-class consultant who always writes excellent executive emails
Zero-shot prompting repeated several times with the same long instruction until one response looks acceptable
Increase the number of examples in a single prompt until the model returns the finished email in one response

stem: A finance team asks a model to work out the total cost of a project with three stages, each with a different discount rule. The model often states a wrong total with no explanation. Which prompting change is most likely to improve accuracy?

choices.text: Provide a single unrelated example about writing a poem so the model learns to follow instructions
Ask the model to work through the problem step by step, showing its reasoning, before it gives the total
Ask the model for the shortest possible answer so that it spends no effort on irrelevant text
Give the model a persona of a certified accountant and tell it to answer with complete confidence

stem: An online retailer wants a customer assistant that can answer "Where is my order and can it still be changed?" The answer depends on live order data held in an internal system, which the model cannot know from training. Which technique fits best?

choices.text: Chain-of-thought prompting alone, asking the model to reason step by step about what an order status could be
Zero-shot prompting with a polite persona, so the model answers courteously whatever it knows about the order
Few-shot prompting with sample orders, so that the model memorizes the status of every customer's current shipment
ReAct prompting, where the model alternates reasoning about what it needs with actions such as calling the order system

stem: A team lead is deciding between chain-of-thought and ReAct prompting for two projects: a tool that checks the logic of a long contract clause using only the text pasted in, and a travel assistant that must check live flight availability while planning. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: ReAct for both, because ReAct is required whenever a task has more than one step to carry out
Chain-of-thought for the contract clause, because the text is self-contained, and ReAct for the travel assistant
Chain-of-thought for both, because reasoning steps alone are enough to retrieve live flight availability
ReAct for the contract clause, because long texts always need tools, and chain-of-thought for the travel assistant

stem: A team added four examples to its prompt for classifying survey comments but wrote no instructions beyond "Here are some examples." Nearly all four examples were positive comments, and the model now labels almost every new comment as positive. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The examples were too few for the foundation model to function at all, so the model returned the same label by default
Zero-shot prompting always overrides examples, so the model ignored the four samples and answered at random
Without clear instructions and with unbalanced examples, the model learned an unintended pattern from the samples
The model has run out of its knowledge cutoff window, so it can no longer analyze the sentiment of recent comments

stem: A retailer wants product descriptions in a specific brand voice. It has about a dozen approved descriptions and needs a working pilot this week, with no machine learning staff available. What is the best first approach?

choices.text: Use few-shot prompting with several approved descriptions and a brand-voice instruction, and test before considering heavier customization
Build a new model from scratch using the descriptions as the full training set, since they define the voice
Fine-tune a foundation model on the approved descriptions and release it to pilot users only after the tuned model is evaluated
Wait until the company has thousands of labeled descriptions, because prompts cannot influence voice at all

stem: An HR team wants the model to draft policy summaries that staff will actually follow. Which TWO additions to a basic prompt are consistent with Google's prompt design guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Removal of all instructions so the model can decide for itself which format the summary takes
A rule that the prompt should never contain context, because extra background always confuses the model
Repetition of the same instruction six times in slightly different words to emphasize it
A statement of the audience, tone and required format, such as plain-language bullets for new employees
One or two short sample summaries that show the expected structure and level of detail

stem: A claims department wants an assistant that handles a complex claim in sequence: read the claim, check each fact against the policy database, decide whether more information is needed, and then draft a decision letter. Which TWO techniques would work together best? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Removing any intermediate output, because showing the steps is unhelpful for tasks that need review
Zero-shot prompting alone, since the policy database is unnecessary when the model has seen insurance documents
A short persona sentence as the only technique, because tone alone determines whether the decision is correct
ReAct prompting, so the assistant can look up policy records through tools while it reasons about the claim
Prompt chaining, so that reading, checking and letter drafting run as connected steps whose outputs feed each other

stem: A team asks a model to solve multi-step scheduling puzzles. Their examples show the final answer first and then a step-by-step explanation written afterward. The model gives confident but wrong answers. Which change is most likely to help?

choices.text: Replace the examples with a request for the final answer in as few words as possible
Reorder the examples so that the reasoning steps come first and the final answer follows from them
Move the examples to a separate earlier prompt so that they are not visible to the model while it works on the puzzle
Add a persona stating that the model is an expert and must never be wrong

stem: A retail bank wants its developers to try several models for a document-summarization project: a Google model, a partner model and an open-weights model. The bank wants to compare them side by side and deploy the winner without building separate integrations for each provider. Which Google Cloud capability fits this need?

choices.text: Model Garden in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, a central catalog where developers discover, test and deploy first-party, partner and open models
Gemini for Google Workspace, which lets each employee choose a preferred model provider inside Docs and Gmail
Agent Search, which gives developers a ready-made search application over the bank's documents and compares model providers automatically
Agent Platform AutoML, which trains and compares candidate models of different providers from the bank's labeled documents

stem: A media company's developers want to run an open-weights model but have no team to provision or operate servers. They want to call it through a managed API. Which approach on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits best?

choices.text: Export the open model to the company's own data center and expose it through an API gateway that the developers operate
Ask Agent Search to import the open model's weights, then publish it as a search widget on the company website
Pick the open model in Model Garden and use it as a Model as a Service offering, which Google serves through a managed API
Train a new open-weights model from scratch with Agent Platform AutoML, so that Google can host the finished model for the company

stem: A subscription retailer has a table of customer history, such as purchases, support tickets and plan type, with a column showing who cancelled. The marketing team wants a model that predicts which customers are likely to cancel. The company has no data scientists and no machine learning engineers. Which option on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which trains a prediction model from the labeled table without requiring data science expertise or code
Agent Search, by indexing the customer table so that marketers can search for customers who look like churners
Model Garden, by deploying a large open language model and asking it to guess churn from each customer's raw row of data
Custom training, where an engineer writes a training application and chooses the algorithm and hyperparameters

stem: A research group wants a model for an unusual scientific objective that is not one of the standard prediction tasks. The group needs its own loss function and full control over the training environment. A colleague proposes Agent Platform AutoML because it is the fastest to set up. What is the best response?

choices.text: Use Agent Search, because it can learn an arbitrary objective from the group's clickstream events
Use Gemini for Google Workspace, because it can train custom scientific models from documents in a shared drive
Use custom training instead, because AutoML only supports predefined objectives and limits control of the training process
Keep AutoML, because it can accept any objective and custom loss function if the group raises its training budget

stem: A software vendor wants customers to find answers on its public documentation website using natural-language questions. The vendor's small web team has little machine learning experience and wants results that include generated summaries with links back to the pages. Which Google Cloud offering is the best fit?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which trains a text classification model from labeled examples that sorts each documentation page into a fixed set of topics for editors
Agent Search, which provides semantic search, generative answers and summaries over the vendor's content, with a widget for the site
Model Garden alone, because choosing a model there automatically indexes the website and adds a search box to it
Custom training of a new language model from scratch on the documentation, hosted by the web team on virtual machines

stem: A streaming service wants viewers to find movies and music through natural-language queries, and wants each viewer to see recommendations tailored to what they watch. The service wants managed capabilities rather than building ranking models itself. Which offering should it evaluate first?

choices.text: A Gemini Enterprise notebook that each editor fills with a playlist for every individual viewer
Contact center agents built with Conversational Agents, which answer phone calls from viewers about their subscriptions
Agent Platform AutoML tabular models only, trained once and queried through a spreadsheet by the editorial team
Agent Search, which includes media search and media recommendations that are tuned for content such as movies, videos and music

stem: An executive asks what RAG Engine in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform does for the company. Which description is most accurate?

choices.text: It permanently retrains the foundation model on the company's documents, so the private knowledge is stored in the model's weights
It filters all prompts for harmful content before they reach the model, and it does not use any company data
It replaces the company's databases with a vector store, which becomes the single system of record for all business data
It connects a model to private data, retrieving relevant passages at question time for better context

stem: A developer team is building a custom assistant on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform that must answer from the company's internal files. Select TWO steps that RAG Engine manages in this process. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replacing the user's question with a fixed answer from a lookup table
Approving each generated answer before it is shown to the user
Ingesting data from sources such as Cloud Storage or Google Drive
Retraining the foundation model's weights on every new document
Indexing the transformed data into a searchable corpus

stem: A company has two projects. The first needs a working question-answering experience over its intranet pages within weeks, with minimal developer effort. The second is a custom application whose developers want to control how data is chunked, which corpus is searched and how retrieved context feeds their own agent logic. Which pairing of Google Cloud RAG offerings matches?

choices.text: Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for the first project, and RAG Engine for the second
Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for both, because only that offering can use company data
Model Garden for the first project, and Agent Platform AutoML for the second
RAG Engine for the first project, and prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for the second

stem: A legal team's assistant, built on a general foundation model, confidently quotes outdated clause wording from its training. The firm's current templates are stored in Cloud Storage and change monthly. The firm does not want to retrain a model every month. Which change addresses the problem?

choices.text: Move the templates to Model Garden, where the platform automatically teaches every hosted model the newest wording from those files
Add RAG: index the templates with RAG Engine so that current clauses are retrieved and supplied to the model with each question
Retrain the foundation model from scratch each month on the new templates so the weights always match them
Lower the response length limit so the assistant has less room to include outdated wording

stem: A software architect describes Agent Development Kit (ADK) to the business sponsor of a new customer-service agent project. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: ADK is an open-source, model-agnostic framework that developers use to build and deploy agents, from simple tasks to complex workflows
ADK is a no-code chat window where business users type instructions and an agent is produced without any developer involvement
ADK is a pre-trained foundation model that Google hosts exclusively for use with the Gemini family
ADK is a billing tool that tracks the usage and cost of each agent after it has been deployed

stem: A developer team has built a custom agent and now needs to run it in production. The company wants Google to handle the infrastructure, scaling and built-in observability so the team can focus on the application. Which part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which hosts any agent code after it trains a prediction model of the agent's behavior on past conversations
A Compute Engine virtual machine group that the team patches, sizes and scales itself
Agent Runtime, a fully managed environment to deploy, operate and scale agents without managing the underlying infrastructure
Agent Search, which converts agent code into a website search widget for the production environment

stem: A company's engineers already use an open-source agent framework they know well and do not want to rewrite their agents. Leadership still wants Google Cloud's managed models, search and grounding services. How does Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform support this?

choices.text: The company must choose between its framework and Google Cloud's grounding services, because the two cannot be used together
Developers may use ADK or any other open-source framework, call Gemini or any model in Model Garden, and use platform services such as RAG
Agent Platform supports only Google-built models, so the company must drop its framework and its other model providers
Only agents written with ADK can access models and services, so the engineers must rewrite their agents before using Agent Platform

stem: An insurance company's CIO is explaining the business value of building agents on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform instead of assembling separate tools. Select TWO statements that are accurate. (Select TWO)

choices.text: The platform requires all company data to be copied into Google's public model training sets before any agent can use it
Using the platform guarantees that an agent will never produce an incorrect answer
Agents built on the platform can use only a single model family chosen at project creation
Agents can be grounded on the enterprise's own data through services such as RAG Engine and Agent Search
One platform covers the full lifecycle: building agents, deploying and scaling them, and governing them

stem: A product team needs two things. First, a model that classifies photographs of building types into categories using the team's own labeled images, with no coding. Second, a way for support staff to ask questions about the team's product manuals and get cited answers. Select TWO products that match these needs, one for each need. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Agent Runtime, for classifying the photographs without any model
Model Garden, for training the image classifier with the team's labeled photographs
RAG Engine, for training the image classifier by chunking the photographs
Agent Search, for natural-language answers over the product manuals
Agent Platform AutoML, for the image classification model trained on the labeled photographs

stem: A manufacturer's leadership team is deciding between Agent Search, RAG Engine and Model Garden for three initiatives. Initiative X is a customer-facing help search with generated answers and an embeddable widget. Initiative Y is a custom agent whose developers want to design retrieval themselves. Initiative Z is a team evaluating which available models write the best product descriptions. Which mapping is correct?

choices.text: X uses Model Garden, Y uses Agent Search, and Z uses RAG Engine
X uses Agent Search, Y uses RAG Engine, and Z uses Model Garden
X, Y and Z all use Model Garden, since every Agent Platform service is accessed through it
X uses RAG Engine, Y uses Model Garden, and Z uses Agent Search

stem: A retailer's AI team wants to test a Google model, an open-source model and a partner model on the same product-description task before committing to one. The CIO wants this comparison done on a single managed platform rather than by stitching together three vendors' tooling. Which strength of Google Cloud's approach addresses this need?

choices.text: An open approach in which Model Garden offers Google, open-source and partner models side by side to discover, test, customize and deploy
An infrastructure-only approach in which Google supplies the servers and the retailer hosts each model with its own tooling
A pre-built application approach in which a finished Google app is configured by users and no model comparison is possible
A closed approach in which every workload must use a single Google-built model, so that results are consistent across all teams

stem: A bank has built agents on a platform that lets it change the underlying model whenever a better or cheaper one appears. The risk team asks what the bank gives up each time the model is changed. Which statement reflects the benefit Google describes for its open, multi-model platform?

choices.text: The bank must rebuild its tool connections and identity policies each time, but gains a better model with every change
The bank can swap only between Google-built models, because partner and open-source models use incompatible controls
The bank can swap models while keeping its underlying logic, tool connections and identity policies intact
The bank can swap models only at the end of a contract term, when Google re-provisions the agents on the new model

stem: A healthcare company wants to use Google's gen AI services with its own confidential documents. Its legal team asks first whether Google will use the company's data to train or fine-tune models without being asked. Which statement describes Google Cloud's enterprise-ready position?

choices.text: Google will use the data only to train models that the company later receives, and never for any other customer's models
Google may use the prompts for training by default and the company must file a request each month to opt out of it
Google does not use customer data to train or fine-tune AI/ML models without the customer's prior permission or instruction
Google lets the company choose training use only after it upgrades from the standard service to a premium support tier

stem: A financial regulator requires a bank to control the encryption keys that protect the data it stores for its gen AI projects, including their location, rotation schedule and who may use them. By default, Google encrypts the content at rest. Which capability meets the requirement?

choices.text: A larger model choice, because bigger models apply stronger encryption to the data they process
A prompt-engineering policy that tells employees not to include sensitive details in the text sent to a model
Google default encryption, which already gives the bank direct control of rotation schedules and key access permissions
CMEK in Cloud KMS, giving the bank control over key protection level, location, rotation and access

stem: A research lab will train a very large model whose computation consists mostly of large matrix operations. The lab asks what Google-designed hardware exists for this. Which hardware, and which benefit, should the cloud adviser describe?

choices.text: General-purpose CPUs only, because matrix-heavy models are best trained on processors built for flexibility with many small tasks
Cloud TPUs, custom chips for large matrix operations with high-bandwidth memory, connectable in slices
Local hard disks on each server, because training speed depends mainly on where the training files are stored
Edge devices at customer sites, because distributing the training across users' phones is how Google scales large models

stem: A media company already has gen AI code written around a popular GPU-oriented framework with many custom operations. Its leaders want to know whether Google Cloud forces a move to Google's own chips. Which description of Google Cloud's AI infrastructure is accurate?

choices.text: Both NVIDIA GPUs and Google Cloud TPUs are offered, so the company can choose the accelerator that fits each workload
Accelerators are offered only on premises, so the company must buy hardware before running its workloads
Only NVIDIA GPUs are offered, because Google's custom chips are reserved for Google's internal products
Only Google's TPUs are offered, so the company must rewrite its code for them before it can use any accelerator

stem: A company plans to train and serve large gen AI models and does not want to assemble accelerators, networking, storage and orchestration software from separate sources. Which Google Cloud offering is described as an integrated supercomputing system optimized for AI and ML workloads?

choices.text: Looker, a business intelligence platform that visualizes data but does not train or serve models
AI Hypercomputer, combining optimized infrastructure, open software and flexible consumption options
Cloud Storage, an object store that holds training data but does not provide accelerators or orchestration
Cloud Run, a serverless service that runs stateless containers and scales them to zero when idle

stem: An operations executive asks which TWO benefits Google associates with AI Hypercomputer for a company that trains and serves gen AI models. (Select TWO)

choices.text: It guarantees that every model it runs is free of bias without any evaluation by the company
It restricts the company to a single framework, which simplifies the choice of software
It maximizes goodput, so accelerators spend more time on productive computation and less on system overhead
It removes the need for any data to be stored, because models learn directly from their prompts
It provides high-throughput storage options that help remove I/O bottlenecks during training

stem: A manufacturer wants employees to ask one question and get answers from content spread across Google Workspace, Microsoft SharePoint, Jira and other business apps. Executives insist that people see only what they are already allowed to see. Which strength of Google's AI ecosystem fits?

choices.text: A data export that copies all files into one shared folder that every employee can open
A public web search that indexes every internal file and shows the same results to all employees regardless of access rights
A separate chatbot per app, so employees must ask each tool individually and combine the results themselves
One Gemini-powered search and assistant with prebuilt connectors to business apps, giving permissions-aware answers

stem: A global company has dozens of teams building agents. The CIO fears "agent sprawl" and wants IT to see, index, manage and reuse agents from one place and enforce consistent policies. Which Google Cloud capability addresses this governance need?

choices.text: A single control plane using Agent Registry and Agent Gateway for central discovery, reuse and policy enforcement
A requirement that all agents be built by one central team so that no other team can build agents
A per-team spreadsheet in which each team lists its agents and applies the policies it prefers
A larger foundation model, because a more capable model automatically enforces company policy on every agent

stem: An auditor reviewing a company's agents asks how the company can trace and audit what each agent did, and limit what each one can access. Which TWO capabilities from Google Cloud's agent platform help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Audit logging is turned off for agents so that sensitive prompts are never written anywhere
All agents share one administrator account, so every action is recorded under the same name
Agents inherit the access of whichever employee created them, with no separate permissions
Each agent receives its own cryptographically secure identity, so its actions can be attributed to it
Least-privilege IAM controls limit what each agent is allowed to access

stem: A marketing team with no programmers wants to build a simple automated process that runs in the background, while the company's engineers want to build more advanced agents in code. Which pair of Google offerings reflects Google's effort to make AI available to both groups?

choices.text: A no-access policy for business users, and a code-only toolkit that is kept for a central research team
A low-code option with templates for business users, and the Agent Development Kit for professional developers
A spreadsheet macro for business users, and a hardware order form for professional developers
A single code-only toolkit for both groups, with business users expected to learn programming first

stem: A small insurer has no data scientists and no budget to train models from scratch, but it wants to add text summarization and image generation to a claims app quickly. Which Google Cloud approach reflects "democratizing AI" for this insurer?

choices.text: Call pre-trained Google models through APIs, customizing them later only if the results need improvement
Wait until a ready-made claims application exists, because gen AI cannot be added to existing apps
Purchase a dedicated accelerator cluster first, then decide which features the app should offer
Collect a large claims dataset and train a custom foundation model before adding any feature to the app

stem: A company worries that its agents will need custom connectors to reach each internal database and business system. Which part of Google Cloud's open approach reduces this effort?

choices.text: A proprietary connector format that works only with systems purchased from Google
A manual process in which an engineer copies data into each agent's prompt every morning
Native support for open standards such as MCP and OpenAPI, so agents connect to existing systems
A requirement to migrate every internal database into a Google-built data store before any agent can use it

stem: A global brand wants to create localized campaigns containing images, audio and video, and the security team insists that all generation happen on one governed enterprise platform instead of several unrelated consumer tools. Which strength of Google Cloud supports this?

choices.text: Google's generative media models, such as Veo, available alongside text models on one secure enterprise platform
A restriction to text generation only, so images, audio and video must be produced outside the platform
A requirement that each campaign team subscribe to a different external tool and upload brand assets to it
A public website where staff paste confidential brand assets so that anyone can view the generated results
